cards.front: What is a buffer, and what must it contain to work?
cards.back: A **buffer** resists pH change when small amounts of acid or base are added. It contains appreciable amounts of a weak acid and its conjugate base (or a weak base and its conjugate acid).
cards.hint: Think about what is needed to react with added acid and added base.

cards.front: In a proton-transfer reaction, what happens to the acid and to the base?
cards.back: The acid donates a proton and becomes its **conjugate base**. The base accepts the proton and becomes its conjugate acid.

cards.front: How does an acetic acid and acetate buffer respond when hydroxide is added?
cards.back: Acetic acid reacts with the added hydroxide: $\mathrm{CH_3COOH+OH^-\rightarrow CH_3COO^-+H_2O}$. This **consumes most of the added base**, so pH changes only slightly.
cards.hint: Name the buffer partner that reacts with OH-.

cards.back: A **spectator ion** remains unchanged during a reaction. It is left out of the net ionic equation.
cards.hint: Na+ that comes with hydroxide is a common example.

cards.front: What are the steps for predicting the products of an acid-base reaction?
cards.back: 1) Identify the proton donor. 2) Remove that proton to form its **conjugate base**. 3) Add the proton to the accepting base to form its conjugate acid. Then check atoms and charge.

cards.front: What are the products when HCl reacts with OH-?
cards.back: $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ and $\mathrm{H_2O}$. The proton from HCl moves to hydroxide to form water.

cards.front: Is water always a product of an acid-base reaction?
cards.back: No. Water forms only when the accepting base is **hydroxide** or the donating acid is **hydronium**. Other reactions can give different products.
cards.hint: Check which species accepts or donates the proton.

cards.front: Write the equation for acetate consuming added hydronium in an acetate buffer.
cards.back: $\mathrm{CH_3COO^-+H_3O^+\rightarrow CH_3COOH+H_2O}$. The acetate is the **conjugate base** that accepts the proton.
cards.hint: Acetate is the buffer partner that accepts H+.

cards.front: Which conjugate pairs appear when hydronium is added to an acetate buffer?
cards.back: $\mathrm{CH_3COOH/CH_3COO^-}$ and $\mathrm{H_3O^+/H_2O}$. The proton moves from hydronium to acetate, forming acetic acid and water.

cards.front: Identify both conjugate acid-base pairs in $\mathrm{NH_3+H_2O\rightleftharpoons NH_4^++OH^-}$.
cards.back: $\mathrm{NH_4^+/NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{H_2O/OH^-}$. Each pair differs by one proton.
cards.hint: Each pair differs by exactly one H+.

cards.front: Can a buffer made from only acetate resist both added acid and added base well?
cards.back: No. Acetate can accept added acid, but with little **acetic acid** present it cannot consume added hydroxide. A buffer needs both conjugate partners.
cards.hint: Which partner reacts with added OH-?

cards.front: Why does a buffer's pH still change slightly when acid or base is added?
cards.back: The reactions **convert some of one partner into the other**, so their relative amounts shift. The buffer removes much of the addition but not all of it.
cards.hint: Think about the ratio of the two partners.
